seoTitle: Free Unicode Character Map: Browse and Copy Symbols
metaDescription: Browse Unicode blocks or any hex range, click a character to copy it, and see its code point, HTML entity and UTF-8 bytes. Free, in your browser.
intro: Lets you browse Unicode by block or by a custom hex range. Click a character to copy it and see its code point, decimal value, HTML entity, UTF-8 bytes and JavaScript escape.
why:
Sometimes you need a character that is not on your keyboard: an arrow, a currency sign, a box-drawing line, a Greek letter or a mathematical operator. Searching the web for one symbol and copying it from a random page is slow, and you rarely get its code point, which is what a developer needs for HTML or source code.

Choose a block such as Arrows or Currency Symbols, or type a hex range. Hover to read the details, click to copy, and use the Jump box to go to a code point or paste a character to find it. Unassigned and control code points are greyed out. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Choose a Unicode block from the list, or enter a custom hex range.
Hover over a character to see its code point and encodings.
Click a character to copy it and add it to the picked tray.
Use Jump with U+1F600 or a pasted character to go to a specific place.

faq.q: What details are shown for a character?
faq.a: The code point in U+ notation, its decimal value, the HTML numeric entity, the UTF-8 bytes in hex and the JavaScript escape. These are the forms you need when writing HTML, CSS or source code.

faq.q: How many characters appear at once?
faq.a: A page shows up to 256 code points, with Prev and Next buttons to move through larger ranges. Unassigned code points, control characters and private use areas are shown disabled.

faq.q: What do combining marks look like?
faq.a: They are displayed on a dotted circle so you can see them alone. When copied they attach to whatever character comes before them in your text.

faq.q: Can I look up a character I only have as text?
faq.a: Yes. Paste it into the Jump box and press Enter. The tool opens the block that contains it and shows its details. For longer text, use the character info tool.
